detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Horsell, Surrey, 1894, is firelight from the left, black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:07. The shot opens on a wide of the road under the burning beeches at night from above the crowd: three hundred people packed across the whole width of the road and every one of them turned the same way, back toward Woking, the front of them already pressing into the backs of those behind, and the fire in the crowns lighting the tops of their heads. The camera is above the crowd at the roadside, a 35mm lens. The burning crowns light them from ABOVE; their hats. At the first frame the packed crowd fills the CENTRE and the BOTTOM two thirds of the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, their hats lit orange along the top. The pale road shows between them in the BOTTOM third, the burning beech crowns run across the TOP third, and black hedges stand at the LEFT edge and the RIGHT edge. The shot is inside this place: the road out of Woking onto Horsell Common at night in 1894: a pale dry road between cut hedges with tall beech trees along its left side, the tops of the beeches alight and burning orange, sparks going up. The camera rises above the crowd with large amplitude until the whole width of the road and the turn of the crowd are inside the picture, travelling one long stride as the crowd turns all together and begins to move back down the road, from 00:00 to 00:04. At 00:04 the movement runs from the front of them to the back like a wave, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:07 the camera is riseing through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
